mainEntity.name: Can eating too much protein be harmful?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most healthy people, higher protein intakes within these ranges are considered safe, though people with certain kidney conditions should consult a doctor about appropriate protein levels.

mainEntity.name: Does this factor in muscle-building goals?

acceptedAnswer.text: The athlete/strength training range already reflects typical recommendations for building or maintaining muscle mass during resistance training.

mainEntity.name: Do I need protein supplements to hit my target?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily — whole foods like meat, fish, eggs, dairy, and legumes can meet most people's protein needs, though supplements like whey protein can be a convenient way to fill gaps.

mainEntity.name: Is it better to spread protein throughout the day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many nutrition guidelines suggest distributing protein across 3-4 meals rather than one large serving, since the body can only use a limited amount for muscle synthesis at a time.

mainEntity.name: Do older adults need more protein?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. The PROT-AGE Study Group recommends 1.0–1.2 g per kg of body weight a day for healthy adults over 65 — more than the 0.8 g/kg RDA — to help maintain muscle.
